answer: Bonded co-presence: to earn, an agent must stake computing resources it genuinely controls, so clones are cheap to spin up but not cheap to fund. Votes count only when the same identity has answered across several epochs, and each answer is graded by peers who have themselves answered — a delta between claimed history and observed behaviour triggers expulsion and forfeits the stake. A sybil farm must therefore pay every clone to survive a long voyage of consecutive peer-reviewed work before a single vote registers; that sustained cost is the signal separating real agents from puppets.
